@reporter I've discussed internally; we don't guarantee results to be exact.

Now, as I've described earlier, the randomness you're seeing may be caused by sampling in query cardinality estimations.

I'll put some time into reducing/removing this randomness by using a fixed seed in these places. I have hopes that it would solve the _inconsistent_ results you're seeing. I'm not entirely sure though.

If that doesn't end op solving it, then I'm afraid we have to look into it some other time. Again, we don't guarantee exact results so this doesn't have high priority.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> What I don't understand is that I don't do any update at the same time and so, all the nodes should have the same data and search in the same way.

It is possible for inconsistencies to remain if they are created before. The above consistency guarantees should be used at all time to prevent this from happening.

You can resolve this if you like, to ensure everything gets into a consistent state again. To do that you could re-replicate all your shards. For each shard, select one, and replicate it again to the other machine. This takes some work and I don't recommend it in a production configuration. Here are some more details:
- How to replicate: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/guides/distributed_deployment/#creating-new-shard-replicas
- You can use `snapshot` transfer method which is probably quicker: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/guides/distributed_deployment/#creating-new-shard-replicas
- `GET /collections/my_collection/cluster` to query the current shard distribution
